title: ESA SPACE WEATHER SERVICE NETWORK PRE-OPERATION, EVOLUTIONARY MAINTENANCE AND DEVELOPMENT
description: The present activity pursues two main objectives.First, it shall ensure the continued high-quality provision of pre-operational space weather services under the existing SWE Service Network. This includes maintaining the availability of the products and servicescurrently included in the Network portfolio through the SWE Service Portal, ensuring the integration of newly developed or updated products, providing first- and second-line end-user support, delivering tailored bulletins to high-priority users, and performing continuous and evolutionary maintenance of key service components.In addition, the service catalogue shall be updated and adapted to reflect emerging and future needs of a European operational space weather service.Second, the activity shall define, design, and implement a modern Research-to-Operations-to-Research (R2O2R) framework for space weather products and services. This shall include the analysis of existing processes, the specification of the target framework, and its practical implementation within the SWE ServiceNetwork.The outcome of the activity shall enable the transition towards a new generation of the SWE Service Network and an updatedversion of the ESA SWE Service Portal.The procurement shall require the application of high standards in software engineering, theactive involvement of end-users within the R2O2R lifecycle, and the delivery of a professional, high-quality user experience for the web portal, including modern software practices, advanced graphical design, and robust human-machine interfaces.

title: IP CORES FOR HIGH-SPEED ADC DAC INTERFACE - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop and verify reusable digital IP cores fully implementing the JESD204B/C high-speed interface standards, addressing current and future high-speed data acquisition and conversion EEE devices. DescriptionNext generation Earth Observation, Telecom and broadly Software-Defined Radio payloads exploit high-speed Analog-to-Digital (ADC) and Digital-to-Analog (DAC) devices, which requirehigh-speed digital interfaces to cope with the throughput demand in the order of gigabit-per-second (Gbps). Furthermore, these devices are thoroughly used in Multiple-Input/Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems, and therefore require synchronisation for simultaneous operation. Two major protocols are JESD204 and ESISTREAM; while the former is an industry standard adopted by many EEE suppliers, thelatter is supported by one supplier.Commercial JESD204 IP cores exist, but they are either open, but prohibitively expensive; locked to a development tool/device vendor; locked to a given ADC/DAC vendor. Furthermore, these IP cores have not been developed with the Space environment in mind, therefore require hardening against single-event effects (SEEs), which may not be possible due to their closed nature. Meanwhile, ESISTREAM IP, is open source and provided free by the supplier, however its' verification status requires improvement and its' adoption is unclear. With many ESA missions and industry products relying on devices having JESD204 interfaces, it is imperative to have verified, SEE-hardened, configurable and device  technology independent IP cores.The provision of aJESD204 IP core covers two different needs simultaneously: interface of ASIC/FPGA with existing EEE components, and a building-block for future EEE ADC/DAC devices. The IP cores will be part of the ESA IP Core's portfolio, making it accessible for future ESA projects and missions, devices and also for smaller companies.Activity encompasses the following tasks: - Study the latest JESD204 standard, derivation of requirements and identification of configurable parameters - Develop verification environment based on Universal Verification Methodology (UVM) - Development of JESD204 IP cores for Transmit and Receive in VHDL, and verification using UVMframework - Development of user-friendly IP core configuration tool for tailoring based on specific device/mode requirements - Synthesis on representative FPGA devices: space-qualified BRAVE, RTG4/PolarFire and COTS (Xilinx) - Trial synthesis for selected ASIC targets - Laboratory demonstrator with representative FPGA and data conversion devices - Produce User Manuals, with integration guidelines

title: ULTRACOMPACT 778 NM RUBIDIUM SECONDARY OPTICAL FREQUENCY STANDARD - EXPRO PLUS
description: The objective of this activity is to develop an ultracompact, secondary, optical frequency reference based on a two-photon transition in Rb vapour at 778nm.Description:Ultra-stable miniature atomic clocks are being considered for space applications. The Rubidium two-photon transition secondary frequency standard has demonstrated interesting performance metrics with a further potential for ultra-low size, weight and power (SWaP) integration.Currently, such an approach is hindered by the lack of miniaturized laser sources with suitable power levels and spectral properties as well as a compact physics package design taking advantage of the full capabilities of the integrated photonics and microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) gas cell technology platforms.This activity aims at exploiting these enabling technologies and developing a further concept of a compact high-performance atomic physics package for an ultra-compact secondary optical frequency standard. The goal of this activity is to provide a fractional frequency stability < 10 - 12 at 1 second integration time implemented using integrated photonic techniques.The following tasks are foreseen in this activity: Evaluate sources of integrated photonic laser systems delivering the wavelengths and the required spectral properties for the defined system approach. Develop Rb cell techniques and technologies targeting an ultracompact 778 nm rubidium secondary optical frequency standard using chip-scale photonic integration. Demonstrate the fractional stability performance achievable using the chosen chip-scale photonic approach. Evaluate chip-scale optical frequency combs with SiN Kerr comb techniques to provide an initial stabilized direct optical-RF link. Provide a packaging solution to maintain the preliminary performance achieved.NOTE: This activityis currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The finallist of participating states will be known at tender issue.

title: CRYOCOOLER ELECTRONICS DEMONSTRATION MODEL VERSATILE FOR MEDIUM CATEGORY CRYOCOOLER - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a versatile demonstration model of Cryocooler Electronics, suitable for a Medium Category Cryocooler.Description: Availability of an off-the-shelf Cryocooler Electronics that is versatile, affordable and readily available could decrease the costs and schedule risks of payloads requiring cryocooled focal planes. Cryocooler Units (CCU) - the full cryocooler delivered assembly - rely on a driver unit called "Cryocooler Electronics" (CCE) that has multiple control functions, such as providing and regulating electrical power, temperature control, micro-vibrations control and launch locking. These CCEs tend to be custom-made for eachcryocooler and mission due to specific needs, such as the cryocooler nature itself, its operating principle, the electrical input power range, bus power interfaces, TM/TC protocol, and other requirements. This bespoke nature makes the CCE a driver in the cryocooler's deliverable critical path and an important barrier to overall Cryocooler Unit affordability. The activity conducts a review of the most relevant use cases, such as Earth Observation optical instrument focal plane cooling, low-earth orbit constellations requiring cryocooling, and space science observatories. The review shall result with identified the main interface requirements and designdrivers that can lead to differentiated CCE designs. The most promising set of interface and functional requirements shall be selected that will render the Versatile CCE with the broadest cross-cutting compatibility across said platforms. Following this a CCE demonstration model design is manufactured and tested. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Reviewing and setting the requirements applicable to the Cryocooler Electronics, referring to multiple use cases and cryocooler natures in the 60W class; - CCE design and breadboard tests - CCE demonstration model manufacturing - CCE demonstration model testing - Way forward for industrialisationDeliverables: Breadboard, Report
